S15.01.note: I did not trace how the button labels the model that Auto routes a message to.
steps: Open the side panel and sign in if asked.
Look at the model button at the right end of the message box bar and read its text.
Open the model button and pick a model under Recommended or All models ($COUNT$).
Close the menu and compare the button text with the model you picked: it should show that model's name, the one the next message uses.
S15.01.where: Side panel > model button at the right end of the message box bar (shows AI Assistant until a model is resolved, then the model name)

S15.02.note: Provider names show only as group headings in All models; the model rows show a logo whose alt text is the raw provider ID, which is not visible.
steps: Open the side panel with a signed-in account.
Click the model button and then All models ($COUNT$).
Read the group headings, which are provider names such as Anthropic or OpenAI.
Compare: each model should sit under the provider that makes it.
S15.02.where: Side panel > model button > All models ($COUNT$)

S15.03.note: The All models list is grouped by provider, not by family; the family helper in managedModelPicker.ts only feeds the hidden locked-model list, so the grouping in Expected is not what the code shows.
steps: Sign in and open the model button.
Click All models ($COUNT$).
Look at the order of the models and the group headings.
Compare: models of one family (all versions of one model line) should sit side by side.
S15.03.where: Side panel > model button > All models ($COUNT$)

S15.07.note: Signed-out users see the note Sign in for models and no Recommended list.
steps: Sign in and open the model button.
Look for the Recommended heading and the short list of models under it.
Click All models ($COUNT$) and check that the Recommended list is replaced by the full list.
Compare the Recommended list with Expected: a short list highlighted for you.

labels.text: Picks the best model for each message

S15.08.note: The Auto row is shown even when signed out, with the Sign in for models note under it.
steps: Open the model button.
Read the first row, named Auto, with the line Picks the best model for each message.
Click Auto and close the menu.
Compare: the button should now show Auto and the next message should be routed automatically.
S15.08.where: Side panel > model button > Auto (first row)

S15.09.note: No separate default-model setting was found; the last model picked is saved and new chats start with it, so compare this with the lasting-default wording in Expected.
steps: Open the model button and pick a model other than Auto.
Click the New chat icon at the top right of the side panel.
Read the model button in the new empty chat.
Compare: the new chat should start with the model you picked. Close and reopen the side panel and check it again.
S15.09.where: Side panel > model button > pick a model > New chat icon in the side panel header (title New chat)

steps: Sign in and open the model button.
Click a specific model under Recommended.
Check that the menu closes and the model button shows that model's name.
Send a short message and compare: the reply should come from the model you chose, which the app shows on the reply.
S15.10.where: Side panel > model button > Recommended or All models ($COUNT$) > click a model

labels.text: Picks the best model for each message

S15.11.note: The grey line is joined from the speed word, the model's best-for text or a capability label; models with no such data show a shorter line or none.
steps: Sign in and open the model button.
Read the grey line under each model name.
Compare: each model should show a short line on what it is good for, such as its speed word and a best-for description.
Note any model whose line is empty or shows only a speed word.
S15.11.where: Side panel > model button > All models ($COUNT$) (or Recommended)

S15.16.note: A model with no speed data shows no speed word.
steps: Sign in and open the model button.
Read the speed word at the start of the grey line under each model: Fastest, Fast, Medium speed or Slower.
Compare: the speed words should show which models are faster or slower.
Check that the Auto row has no speed word.
S15.16.where: Side panel > model button > Recommended or All models ($COUNT$)

S15.18.needs: a signed-in account on a lower plan
S15.18.note: Locked rows appear only in All models; the visible text is the plan name, and the full available-on sentence is only in the row's accessible name.
steps: Sign in with a plan below the top tier.
Open the model button and click All models ($COUNT$).
Look for rows with a plan name on the right, such as Premium, and read the plan name.
Click one locked row and compare: a new tab should open on the pricing page.
S15.18.where: Side panel > model button > All models ($COUNT$)

S15.22.note: Some effort rows may be greyed out with a plan name; which models expose Effort was not checked against live data.
steps: Pick a model that has effort options (the Effort heading only appears for those).
Open the model button and find the Effort heading with its rows (for example Direct, Brief, Quick, Balanced, Deep, Extended, Maximum).
Click a different effort row and close the menu.
Compare: the model button should now show that effort word beside the model name, and the Default badge should mark the default row.
S15.22.where: Side panel > model button > pick a reasoning model > Effort heading

S15.29.note: The choice is saved in browser storage on this device; switching to a different account resets it to Auto.
steps: Open the model button and click a model other than Auto.
Close the side panel completely.
Reopen the side panel and read the model button.
Compare: it should show the same model you picked before closing.
S15.29.where: Side panel > model button > Recommended > pick a model; then close and reopen the side panel

S15.30.note: Chats must be saved to appear under Recent chats.
steps: Pick model X in the model button, then send a message in a chat.
Click the New chat icon, pick model Y, and send a message in the new chat.
Click the Recent chats clock icon and open the first chat.
Compare: the model button in the reopened chat should show model X, not model Y.
S15.30.where: Side panel > Recent chats (clock icon in the header) > open a chat; New chat icon in the header
